audience: A student who has just finished ONE first course in linear algebra (vectors, matrices, matrix multiplication, linear systems and Gaussian elimination, determinants, inverses, eigenvalues and eigenvectors of small matrices, the dot product, orthogonality and projections) plus single-variable calculus (derivatives, integrals, Taylor polynomials, exponentials and logarithms). Everything else - multivariable calculus, optimization, probability and statistics, dynamical systems and control, reinforcement learning, neural networks, functional analysis - must be built up inside the section before a module relies on it.

primers.title: Mathematical Language, Proofs & Limits
primers.subtitle: Sets, quantifiers, functions, proof techniques, limits, suprema, compactness and O-notation
sections: set-builder notation, membership, subsets, unions/intersections (also indexed families), complements and set differences, cardinality, Cartesian products, quantifiers and why their ORDER matters (for all x there exists y vs there exists y for all x), implications, contrapositive, negating statements, "iff", "without loss of generality"

domain/codomain, image and preimage, composition, injective/surjective/inverse, functions of several variables, sets defined by functions (level sets {x : h(x) >= 0}), set-valued maps and operators on sets, fixed points and fixed-point iteration, monotone set operators and their limits

direct proof, contrapositive, contradiction, induction (incl. induction over time steps as in safety proofs), counterexamples, "it suffices to show", chaining inequalities, how to read a theorem (assumptions -> conclusion) and check that every assumption is used

sequences and convergence, limits of functions, monotone bounded sequences, the geometric series and discounting sum_t gamma^t = 1/(1-gamma), telescoping sums, the exponential and log as limits, convergence rates (linear, sublinear)

upper/lower bounds, sup and inf vs max and min, sup over infinite sets, properties (sup of a sum, sup of a scaled set), extended reals and +/- infinity, liminf/limsup (brief), "almost everywhere/almost surely" as a preview

distance and balls in R^n, open and closed sets, interior and boundary (why the boundary {h = 0} matters for safety), closure, bounded and compact sets, continuous functions attain max/min on compact sets (Weierstrass), uniform continuity, neighbourhoods and "locally"
O, Omega, Theta, o, soft-O (tilde-O), what "sample complexity" and "regret sublinear in T" mean, logarithmic factors, comparing rates like T^{1/2}, T^{2/3}, log^3 T
iterate x_{k+1} = g(x_k) for adjustable contractions, watch convergence and the geometric error bound; partial sums of the discounted series sum gamma^t

primers.title: Linear Algebra II: Norms, Positive Definiteness & the SVD
primers.subtitle: From a first linear algebra course to the matrix tools every later module uses
sections: inner products, Cauchy-Schwarz (with proof), l1/l2/l_inf norms, triangle inequality, unit balls, distances and metrics, balls B_r(x)
induced norms ||A|| = max ||Ax||/||x||, spectral norm, Frobenius norm, submultiplicativity ||AB|| <= ||A|| ||B||, norm of a product of layers, why norms bound how much a map can stretch
real eigenvalues, orthonormal eigenvectors, A = Q Lambda Q^T, Rayleigh quotient, lambda_min / lambda_max as min/max of x^T A x on the unit sphere, spectral radius

definition x^T P x >= 0, equivalent tests (eigenvalues, Sylvester minors, Cholesky), Gram matrices K = Phi^T Phi are PSD, the Loewner order A >= B, congruence T^T M T, ellipsoids {x : x^T P x <= 1}, matrix square roots, sums/scaling of PSD matrices, the PSD cone
A = U Sigma V^T, geometry (unit circle to ellipse), singular values vs eigenvalues of A^T A, spectral norm = sigma_max, rank, condition number, pseudo-inverse, power iteration
Block Matrices, Determinants, Trace & log det

block multiplication, block inverses, the Schur complement (first look; Module 2 does the LMI version), matrix inversion (Woodbury) lemma, determinant of block matrices, trace and tr(AB) = tr(BA), log det and its meaning (volume), det(I + A B) = det(I + B A)

orthogonal matrices and rotations/reflections, skew-symmetric matrices, the Cayley transform (preview), diagonal and permutation matrices, Toeplitz/circulant matrices and convolution as matrix multiplication, Kronecker/vectorization only if needed
Functions as Vectors: Inner Product & Hilbert Spaces

vector spaces of functions, inner products of functions, orthonormal bases and coefficients, infinite dimensions, completeness (what a Hilbert space adds), feature maps and kernels k(x,y) = <phi(x), phi(y)>, why Gram matrices of kernels are PSD - the bridge to RKHS in Module 3
Interactive: Quadratic Forms, Eigenvectors & the SVD
2x2 matrix sliders; unit circle mapped to an ellipse; eigenvectors, singular vectors, PSD test, level sets of x^T P x

primers.title: Calculus, Convexity & Optimization
primers.subtitle: Gradients, Lipschitz continuity, convex sets and functions, descent methods and constraints
sections: Gradients, Jacobians, Hessians & the Chain Rule
partial derivatives, gradient, directional derivative, Jacobian, Hessian, multivariable chain rule (and backpropagation as the chain rule), first/second-order Taylor expansion, mean value theorem
gradients of linear and quadratic forms, of ||Ax - b||^2, of log det X (= X^{-1}) and tr(AX), derivative of X^{-1}, gradients with respect to matrices

definition, Lipschitz constant as a bound on the gradient norm, composition rule L(f o g) <= L(f) L(g), local vs global, Hoelder continuity, moduli of continuity, L-smooth functions, why Lipschitz bounds give safety margins

convex sets (balls, half-spaces, polyhedra, ellipsoids, the PSD cone), convex functions, first- and second-order conditions, Jensen's inequality, strong convexity, sublevel sets, convex conjugates and the Fenchel inequality (brief)
Gradient Descent, Newton's Method & Step Sizes
gradient descent and step sizes, convergence on smooth convex functions (statement), stochastic gradients, Newton's method, momentum (brief), gradient ascent for maximization
Constraints: Lagrange Multipliers, Projections, Penalties & Barriers

equality constraints and Lagrange multipliers, inequality constraints and complementary slackness (intuition; KKT in Module 2), projection onto convex sets, projected gradient, penalty methods, log-barrier / interior-point idea, feasibility
LP and QP standard forms, geometry of the feasible set, a QP with one half-space constraint solved in closed form (projection onto a half-space), solvers as black boxes

argmax/argmin sets (possibly empty or non-unique), optimizing over infinite sets (building on sup/inf from Primer 0), exchanging max and min, saddle points and two-player games (preview of duality, robust control and adversarial training)
a 2-D objective with a constraint; gradient descent, projected gradient and log-barrier paths

primers.title: Probability, Concentration & Information
primers.subtitle: Random variables, Gaussians, high-probability guarantees, martingales, KL divergence and risk measures
sections: sample spaces and events (informal), discrete and continuous random variables, densities and CDFs, expectation and linearity, variance, covariance matrices (they are PSD), independence, indicator functions, law of large numbers (statement)
conditional probability, Bayes' rule, conditional expectation and the tower rule, likelihoods and posteriors (Bayesian updating)
Markov Chains, Stationary Distributions & Monte Carlo

Markov chains and transition matrices, stationary distributions (as eigenvectors), noisy dynamical systems x_{t+1} = a x_t + w_t and their stationary variance, Monte Carlo estimation, standard errors of means and proportions (vs confidence intervals), almost-sure statements and supports
univariate and multivariate normal, affine transformations, marginals, conditioning formula via the Schur complement (the engine of GP regression), the standard normal CDF Phi and quantiles
Concentration: Markov, Chebyshev, Hoeffding & Sub-Gaussian Noise
Markov, Chebyshev, Chernoff/Hoeffding (with proof sketch), sub-Gaussian random variables (definition via the MGF), bounded noise is sub-Gaussian, Gaussian tails
"With Probability at Least 1 - delta": Union Bounds & Confidence Statements
reading high-probability guarantees, the union bound over many events and over time, confidence intervals, frequentist vs Bayesian guarantees, what 'uniformly over all t and x' adds

why data chosen by an algorithm is not i.i.d., filtrations as 'what is known at time t', martingales and martingale differences, Azuma-Hoeffding (statement), the idea of self-normalized bounds (method of mixtures, intuition only; Module 3 uses it)
Entropy, KL Divergence, Total Variation & Mutual Information

entropy (discrete and differential), KL divergence and its non-symmetry, total variation distance, Pinsker's inequality, f-divergences (brief), mutual information and the Gaussian formula 1/2 log det(I + sigma^{-2} K)
quantile functions, VaR, CVaR and the Rockafellar-Uryasev formula, tail conventions (alpha vs 1 - alpha), chance constraints vs expected-value constraints

Bernoulli and binomial distributions, binomial tail bounds and Clopper-Pearson intervals, hypothesis testing, false alarm vs missed detection, the Neyman-Pearson lemma (statement), exchangeability and the rank argument used by conformal prediction
sample means vs Hoeffding/Chebyshev bounds; 2-D Gaussian conditioning with the Schur complement

primers.title: Dynamical Systems, Stability & Feedback Control
primers.subtitle: State-space models, Lyapunov stability, invariant sets, frequency response, LQR, PID and MPC
sections: continuous time dx/dt = f(x,u) and discrete time x_{k+1} = f(x_k,u_k), flows and trajectories, existence and uniqueness (Lipschitz vector fields), forward completeness, equilibria, linearization via the Jacobian, sampling a continuous-time system
x_{k+1} = A x_k and dx/dt = A x, matrix powers and the matrix exponential, Schur and Hurwitz stability via eigenvalues, spectral radius, modes, inputs and outputs (A, B, C, D)
Lyapunov Functions, Invariant Sets & Regions of Attraction

stability definitions (Lyapunov, asymptotic, exponential), Lyapunov's direct method in continuous and discrete time, quadratic Lyapunov functions and the Lyapunov equation, sublevel sets, forward invariance, region of attraction, Nagumo's condition (intuition)
class-K, extended class-K and class-KL functions, the comparison lemma for scalar differential inequalities, how it turns dh/dt >= -alpha(h) into h(t) >= 0 (preview of Module 10)
Feedback Control: State Feedback, LQR & PID
closing the loop u = Kx, the LQR problem and the Riccati equation (statement), PID control and integral action (zero steady-state error), controllers as policies
Transfer Functions, Frequency Response, Gains & Parseval

z- and Laplace transforms (working knowledge), transfer functions, frequency response, the L2 / l2 gain and the H-infinity norm, Parseval's theorem, FIR filters and convolution as LTI systems, why frequency-domain inequalities appear in the KYP lemma and IQCs
Feedback with Nonlinearities: Lur'e Systems & Sector Conditions
Lur'e systems (linear plant + static nonlinearity), sector and slope conditions, loop transformations, small-gain theorem, circle and Popov criteria (statements), where neural-network activations fit
controllability and observability, the controllability Gramian and the Lyapunov equation, realizing a transfer function / FIR filter as (A, B, C, D), 2-D (Roesser) systems in one paragraph

cost-to-go and the dynamic programming principle, Bellman/HJB equations (viscosity solutions as a black box), backward reachable sets, receding-horizon MPC, terminal sets and recursive feasibility, invariant-set algebra (Minkowski sum, Pontryagin difference) and tube MPC in one page
2-D linear system with eigenvalue sliders; trajectories, Lyapunov level sets and a saturated nonlinear variant

primers.title: MDPs, Reinforcement Learning & Neural Networks
primers.subtitle: Policies, value functions, Bellman equations, policy gradients, and the neural networks inside them
sections: multi-armed and continuous bandits, simple vs cumulative regret, exploration vs exploitation, optimism (UCB), acquisition functions (UCB, expected improvement, entropy search) and the Bayesian-optimization loop with a GP surrogate (preview of Modules 3-5), multi-objective trade-offs and Pareto fronts (brief)
states, actions, transitions, rewards and costs, stochastic policies, trajectories, discounted and average returns, the Markov property, episodes
V, Q, advantage A, Bellman expectation and optimality equations, discounted state-visitation (occupancy) distributions and their normalization (the 1/(1-gamma) factor)
value iteration and its contraction argument, policy iteration, the tabular setting, from DP to learning
the policy gradient theorem, score-function estimator, baselines and advantages, natural gradient and Fisher information (intuition), TRPO/PPO trust regions via KL, why step sizes matter for safety
Q-Learning, Actor-Critic, Entropy Regularisation, Model-Based & Offline RL

Q-learning and DQN, actor-critic, SAC and entropy regularisation (soft Bellman), learned dynamics models and ensembles, model-based RL, offline RL and distribution shift, reward models / RLHF in one paragraph
affine layers W x + b, activations (ReLU, tanh, sigmoid, GroupSort/MaxMin) and their slopes, the network as a composition, training by gradient descent and backpropagation
convolution layers as structured matrices (channels, kernels, stride), residual connections, recurrent networks as dynamical systems, equilibrium (implicit) layers and fixed points
logits and margins, adversarial perturbations in l2 / l_inf balls, certified radius from a Lipschitz bound, clean vs certified accuracy
Interactive: Value Iteration & a Tiny Network
gridworld value iteration step by step; a 2-2-1 network with its decision boundary, margin and a Lipschitz-based certified radius
